mission: Galley. Torin brings up the bad thing over food, as he always does. He uses the Valley's destabilisation as evidence the seal was always temporary. The only permanent answer, he argues, is someone who understands the technique becoming the new seal. Then: 'You're curating reality to manage the outcome you want. You know who else did that?'
why_now: The widening crisis gives Torin the argument he has been waiting to make. It also gives Ben no room to dismiss the observation that comes with it, because the observation is accurate.
conflict: Torin makes his argument with warmth and devastating specificity. He is not trying to seize power; he is offering to pay a price. The horror is in the nobility of it — Jacen's pattern wearing a better mask — and in the line Torin says next, which describes Ben's own behaviour without naming Jacen.
turning_point: Torin's observation about curating reality lands. Ben cannot dismiss it because it is true. The question the chapter will answer in sc3 is whether recognising the pattern is enough to break it.
opening_hook: Torin brings it up over food. He always brings the worst things up over food — it's a disarming technique Ben is starting to recognize.
closing_hook: The observation about curating reality lands like a blade. Ben can't dismiss it because Torin is right — Ben IS withholding, controlling information, managing the narrative. The question is whether recognizing the pattern is enough to break it.
emotional_trajectory: Engaged debate -> seductive logic -> the devastating personal parallel

stakes.personal: Ben's own pattern of control named by the person repeating it at larger scale
stakes.interpersonal: Torin and Ben — mutual respect making the disagreement more painful
stakes.external: Torin's 'solution' would work but at the cost of everything the group has been building

setting: Aboard the Steady Returns — common area, meal time
sensory_details: Food cooling between them as the argument sharpens; Torin's warmth carrying on schedule rather than by weather; Sera's silence with the weight of having heard this argument before; Ben's hands under the table, finding his own knees
action_beats: Torin pushes his plate aside and pulls the tactical display between them as he makes his argument
Ben's hands grip his knees under the table as Torin names the pattern — curating reality to manage outcomes
Sera sits motionless through the exchange, her silence carrying the weight of having heard this argument before
notes: H15 planted — Torin's observation about curating reality. It must land as true, not melodramatic — warmth, timing, and specific accuracy. Torin's arc: lie_deepened — his certainty growing as the crisis validates his analysis. Anti-pattern: Torin's 'you know who else did that' must stop there. No one names Jacen in this scene; Ben does the naming in Ch18. Diagnostic-voice trap — Ben should not, in this scene, inwardly complete the Jacen identification. His hands grip his knees; the sentence sits on the air; Sera's silence carries it. Interiority paragraphing the recognition would give back everything the chapter is trying to keep tight.
